models.invocation.noticePurged: A received native response or rejection is evidence only; it is neither task acceptance nor a billing determination. This invocation counts toward the total call quota; retry the same command identity to return its receipt without resending. Response content has been logically purged; human output never shows response content.
models.invocation.notice: A received native response or rejection is evidence only; it is neither task acceptance nor a billing determination. This invocation counts toward the total call quota; retry the same command identity to return its receipt without resending. Response content, if captured, is retained separately from the receipt and withheld by default. JSON includeResponseContent additionally requires inspect-content permission; human output never shows retained response content.

identity.help:
Usage: deckent identity [--scope <id>]            status: selected profile (or how to select one), people, roles
       deckent identity profiles [--verbose] [--registry <file>] [--json]
       deckent identity preview [--profile <namespace:id>] --scope <id>
         [--profile-version <n>] [--input <file|->] [--registry <file>] [--json]
profiles: one line per profile with its meaning; digests with --verbose.
Input: members, organization, assignments, removeBindingIds; optional
projectScopeIds and includeFutureProjects. Registry: custom package array.
Preview only; no authority, deployment, identity verification or model call.
Without --profile the installation's identity.profile is used; when none is
selected the command says so: select one with deckent config set identity.profile.
Usage: deckent identity choices --scope <id>
       deckent identity distribute --input <selection-file|-> [--json]
       deckent identity distribute --apply --input <submission-file|->
         --expect <preview-digest> [--json]
       deckent identity distribute --scope <id> [--apply]
On a terminal, distribute picks profile, person, role and scope with the arrow keys
and shows the preview on a card before anything is applied.
Apply requires an admin, an attested terminal and existing identities.
identity.distributionHelp:
Usage: deckent identity choices --scope <id>
       deckent identity distribute --input <selection-file|-> [--json]
       deckent identity distribute --apply --input <submission-file|->
         --expect <preview-digest> [--json]
       deckent identity distribute --scope <id> [--apply]
Selection: schemaVersion=1, profile, scopeId, assignments
(principalId, roleId, scopeIds), removeBindingIds. Use catalog choices.
On a terminal, profile, person, role and scope are picked with the arrow keys and
the preview is shown on a card before --apply writes anything.
Apply requires an admin, an attested terminal and existing identities.
Keep the preview submission envelope for exact replay; preview grants
no authority. Current separation-of-duties rules remain in force.

climodels.roles.help:
Usage: deckent models roles [show] [--channel <id> [--model <exact id>]] [--scope <id>] [--json] [--lang en|tr]
       deckent models roles set --channel <id> --model <exact id> --tier worker|frontier (--roles <role,role> | --no-roles) [--command-id <id>] [--scope <id>] [--lang en|tr]
Which exact catalog model may serve which role (Brain, worker, recovery decision, memory evaluator). A model the catalog lists but no row names is
pending: no role may use it until a person gives it a tier and roles. show lists every catalog model the scope sees with its maker, tier, roles
and state. set opens one card on your own terminal (never an AI tool, pipe or --json): channel, exact model id, catalog maker and price, the row
now and the proposed row, and what it unlocks. Apply writes one row to the installation (global) model_roles overlay by compare-and-set; the
change is audited like every governed setting and applies without a restart. A tier only makes a model eligible; the scope still has to
activate it (deckent models activate).
